Beta 2 of 2.4: interface styles. A theme can now change how the console is built, not only its colours: keep the hardware you know, flatten it, strip it down to plain blocks, or turn every part into a sticker. Beta 1 brought the Simple theme editor. Betas are offered only to people who turned on Receive beta updates.
### Added
- **Interface styles.** Every theme now has a style, which decides how the keys, panels, faders and the case itself are drawn and how a key answers a press. There are four. Real Hardware is the console as it has always been. Flat Hardware sits each key on its own darker base, with no sockets and short shadows. Soft Blocks is flat colour with rounder corners, no outlines and no shadows, and a key squashes slightly when pressed. Sticker gives every part a thick outline and a hard shadow, like a die cut sticker, and a pressed key drops onto its shadow. The display, the album art and the layout stay the same in every style. - **Choose a style in either editor.** Simple has a STYLE row above MATERIAL. Advanced has the same four keys at the top of Interface. The whole console changes as you choose, and the theme browser names a theme's style beside it when it is not Real Hardware. - **Funhouse.** A new built-in theme made for Sticker, after a sheet of retro stickers: a sky blue case with mustard keys and hot pink for what is on. In dark it becomes a deep blue sheet with the same mustard keys. - **Sticker Ink.** A new colour in the Advanced editor, beside Key Print, for the outline and hard shadow of the Sticker style. Left alone, it follows Primary Text on a light theme and Key Print on a dark one. - **Simple theme editor.** Press NEW in the theme browser or in the editor to start a theme from the colours of the one you are using. Enter two to six colours and CrateDigger decides which one paints the frame, the panels, the text, the accent, the screen glass and the screen text, and works out every other colour from them. Hover a colour to see what it paints. - **Shuffle.** SHUFFLE tries another arrangement of the same colours. The arrow keys step back and forward through your last 20 steps, colour changes included. Pin a colour to a job to keep it there while you shuffle. - **Readable whatever you pick.** Text, key labels, selected rows and the display always keep enough contrast against what they sit on. CONTRAST sets how much: Soft, Standard or High. A pale screen glass becomes a one colour LCD, the way Llama '97's does. - **One palette, light and dark.** APPEARANCE builds a Light theme, a Dark theme or Both from the same colours. - **Presets for the rest.** MATERIAL picks the shell's finish, ALBUM ART picks the LCD look of the compact and mini players' art, and three rows of font presets set the screen titles, the labels and readouts, and the interface type. - **A preview that shows what goes where.** Simple draws the full window, the mini player and the compact player in your colours, with the album art run through the same LCD screen the players use. The app keeps your current theme until you press APPLY. - **Preview in Advanced.** The full token editor is now called ADVANCED, and its new PREVIEW key shows the mini player and the compact player while you edit. - **Accent Key Print.** A new colour in the Advanced editor, under Buttons & Knobs, for the labels printed on accent coloured keys, so they can differ from the text of selected rows. The built-in themes look exactly as before.
### Changed
- **Llama '97 and Pocket wear Flat Hardware.** Both built-in themes change shape with this update. Llama '97's light look is also recoloured after the classic skin: a lavender grey case, pale grey keys, black lists in mint green and yellow column headers. Its dark look keeps its colours. To get the old shape back, make a copy of the theme in the editor and choose Real Hardware. Carbon and Cobalt look exactly as before, and so does any theme you made or installed. - **Key Print reaches every small key.** A theme that sets its own Key Print now gets it on the VIEW, THEME and EQ labels, the small keys in the panel headers and the mini player's keys, which used to borrow a text colour meant for panels. A theme saved from Advanced after its secondary text colour was changed may show those small labels in its earlier secondary colour; set Key Print to choose. - **FLAT is for Real Hardware.** The other three styles draw their own shadows, so the FLAT switch is dimmed while one of them is chosen and comes back, as you left it, with Real Hardware. - **Moving between Simple and Advanced asks first.** A Simple theme can be copied to Advanced or converted; a converted theme can't go back to Simple. An Advanced theme, a built-in included, can be copied into Simple. - **The status lamp is a key.** The lamp at the top right that steps through the display animations now sits in a small key that lights when you point at it and goes down when pressed, so it reads as something you can click.
### Fixed
- **Devices saved by a newer version are kept.** If a later version of CrateDigger saved a kind of device this one doesn't know, this version now keeps it, instead of losing every saved device the next time it saves one.

Beta 1: Relocate Library points your crates at music you copied or moved to another drive yourself. Betas are offered only to people who turned on Receive beta updates.
### Added
- **Relocate Library.** If you copied or moved your music to another drive or folder outside CrateDigger, Preferences, General now has Relocate Library. Choose the folder the music is in now, and every track with a copy at the same place inside it is pointed there, along with its crates, play counts and ratings. The old drive does not have to be connected, unless your Crates Index is on it. It asks once before changing anything and never moves or deletes a file. Tracks with no copy stay where they are, and the Music Folder follows when it was the old one.
